findings.issue: The app ships with zero tests and no test tooling, despite containing ~880 lines of untested filtering, pagination, sorting and data-mapping logic.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (already on the Vite toolchain) with unit tests for the pure helpers in src/lib/api.js and the route-handler transforms, plus a Playwright smoke test per page.

findings.issue: compareRows handles missing values inside `result` before the direction flip, so on a descending sort missing Power/Accuracy/PP sort first, violating the spec's 'missing values sort last in both directions'. The acceptance suite never caught it and no test would.
findings.suggestion: Return early for missing values without negating, and add a unit test with mixed missing/numeric rows asserting missing-last in both directions.

findings.issue: The catch block maps every error — including 5xx API failures and network faults — to a 404 'Not found' page, masking real outages as 'resource does not exist'.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish ApiError.status 404 from other errors; render Not found only for 404 and a 500 page otherwise. Add tests for both paths.

findings.issue: Live filtering re-fetches the full page HTML and swaps in getElementById('home-results'); the race guard and the hard-coded element id are untested, and a template refactor that renames the id silently kills live search with no failing test.
findings.suggestion: Extract the request-id guard and fragment swap into a small tested module, or assert the id exists at build time; test stale-response ordering.

findings.issue: homeHref and the handler's page clamping (min(positiveInteger(page), totalPages), default-omission rules) implement the URL-state contract entirely untested; an off-by-one or an omitted-default regression breaks deep links like /?type=fire&generation=generation-i&page=2.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test homeHref against the spec's URL cases (empty q, page 1, invalid page, unknown type/generation values).

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavorText encodes two spec rules (last English entry, whitespace collapsed to one space); swapping the reverse iteration for .find() or dropping the \s+ replace would pass review unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests with \n/\f runs and non-English trailing entries.

findings.issue: uniqueSpeciesFromPokemonReferences performs dedupe, alternate-form exclusion (id >= 10000) and dex-number sort for three different pages; a change to idFromUrl's regex (api.js:59-63) or the filter would silently drop or add species on ability/type/move pages.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests covering ids 10001+, duplicate references, and unordered input.

findings.issue: Evolution rendering is recursive (buildEvolutionTree/renderEvolutionNode); branching chains like Eevee and empty/missing chain nodes are exercised only by manual browsing.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test buildEvolutionTree against a branching fixture (Eevee) and a species with no chain.

findings.issue: The in-memory promise cache (set-then-catch-delete) is untested; a refactor could cache rejected promises or never evict failures, turning one transient API hiccup into a permanently broken page.
findings.suggestion: Test that a failed getJson can be retried successfully and that concurrent calls share one fetch.

findings.issue: The BUILDING() env-guard pattern (returning {} at build time) is repeated in every route handler and interacts with Gracile's prerender step; nothing verifies the production build actually skips fetching.
findings.suggestion: One build-time assertion or test that `npm run build` completes without hitting the API.

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no test files — leaving ~880 lines of hand-rolled filtering, pagination, URL-state, sorting and data-mapping logic guarded only by the acceptance suite. That suite already misses real issues: descending sort puts missing values first (a spec violation) and any API error on a Pokémon page renders as 404. Pure-function tests for src/lib/api.js and the route transforms would have caught both and are the cheapest insurance this codebase could get.
